newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt mixed but volume low ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mixed but volume low ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: Brady bond prices were mixed on Monday, but volume remained thin with investors reluctant to make any major moves before the slew of U.S. data due this week, traders said.

"There is a lot of U.S. data coming out this week so, that may restrict movement in either direction...I am expecting quite a quiet week until the end of the week when all the numbers are out," said a Brady bond trader at a U.S. investment bank.
Key U.S. economic reports include the second-quarter employment cost index on Tuesday, second-quarter real GDP on Thursday and July unemployment on Friday.

Dollar-denominated instruments should continue to move higher if U.S. jobs data prove bond-friendly, but some Brady bond traders remained cautious before the data because any downturn in the U.S. Treasury market would have a spillover effect.
"We have (U.S.) labor market news, and the market may trade down on that," said one Brady bond trader at a major U.S. investment bank in London.
Analysts said floating-rate bonds would fare better than fixed-rate instruments if the U.S. Treasury market turned lower.
"Russian Vnesh and Prins still offer reasonable value given that they are floaters, and they are less likely to be affected by the Treasury market than the others," an emerging market trader said.
Among Eastern European Brady bonds, Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 1/4 lower ar 76-1/2 bid and Polish PDI bonds PO325024=RR were 1/8 firmer at 87-1/8.
In the Latin Brady market, Ecuadorean debt continued to firm after news last week the country received a B-1 rating from Moody's Investors Service Inc.
Ecuadorean pars ECPARS=RR were 1/4 higher at 53-5/8 bid and the country's PDI bonds ECPDI=RR were 1/8 higher at 70-1/2 bid.
